newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks forge ahead, further gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks forge ahead, further gains seen.

text.p: Croatian stocks forged ahead on Wednesday with hoteliers leading the way, and traders predicted further gains in most issues this week thanks to strong demand.
But some said light profit taking was on the cards for a few as investors reap some of recent gains before a correction.
"Who knows what will happen next week, but for this week I expect further growth," said Josko Milisa of brokerage I.F.C.
He said continued buying interest and involvement of foreign players could drive stocks like cable maker Elka and Istrian hotelier Laguna even higher, with others joining the trend.
Higher supply of confectioner Kras shares, however, might indicate a downward slide from the current peak before long.
Blue chip Pliva was again not traded and its global depositary receipts (GDRs), issued at 50 to each share, headed down to $47.87/435 on the London Stock Exchange.
* Seven of 10 active issues rose, one edged down and two were unchanged.
* The only loser was Podravka, closing two kuna down at 275 after a mixed trade on volume of 2,103 shares.
* Laguna led gainers, leaping 350 kuna to end at a new high of 1,450 kuna with 260 shares sold. It was followed by:
- Kras, up 49 kuna to 729, also overshooting previous records. It sold 1,455 shares.
- Hotelier Istraturist, selling 270 units, rose 40 kuna to 270.
- Dalmatian tourist firm Suncani Hvar, added 24 to 80 kuna. It was also the most actively traded with 6,949 shares.
- Arenaturist and Elka rose 20 kuna to 270 and 240 kuna, respectively with 1,016 and 228 shares sold.
* Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka was flat at 1,000 kuna on volume 2,189. Its GDRs, representing 1/10 of each share, traded at $18.875 on Seaq International in London.
- Also unchanged was hotelier Riviera, at 280 kuna after a steep rise last and early this week, with 128 shares sold.
* Volume up at 14,690, turnover lower at 5.0 million kuna.
